reading.title: Math at the Carpenter's Bench
reading.purpose: See how carpenters and builders use geometry and measurement words on real projects.
paras: Step into a wood shop, and you will see math at work. Builders do not just saw boards. They check shapes, measure sides, and solve math steps before they make one cut.

Say a builder plans a wood frame. First, they find the perimeter, the full length all the way round the edge. Each corner needs a neat right angle where two boards meet. If left and right trims match like two halves, the frame has symmetry.

Before buying wood, a builder will calculate the full length they need, using math to get the sum. An approximate guess, close to the true size, works fine when pricing pine. When cutting glass, though, the size must be exact, right down to the last tiny mark.

Shops also track counts and limits. A box tag lists the quantity, or count, of nails inside. A tall step stool prints its maximum weight, the most load it can hold. A glue jar lists the minimum wait time, the least time it needs to dry. To drill a tight spot, a builder may rotate a board round its mid point.
Smart math turns rough boards into neat work that fits just right.

choices: the total distance all the way around a shape
the greatest weight a wooden ladder can hold
the total number of metal screws inside a box
the smallest drying time printed on a bottle
qs.why: Paragraph 2 defines perimeter as "the total distance all the way around the outside edge."

qs.q: Which sentence shows when a builder needs an exact size?
choices: Before buying wood, a builder will calculate the full length they need, using math to get the sum.
An approximate guess, close to the true size, works fine when pricing pine.
When cutting glass, though, the size must be exact, right down to the last tiny mark.
Smart math turns rough boards into neat work that fits just right.
qs.why: This sentence specifies that cutting glass requires an exact size down to the last tiny mark.

ev.text: When cutting glass, though, the size must be exact, right down to the last tiny mark.

qs.q: Why is it smart to check a step stool's maximum weight before climbing?
choices: It tells the most load the stool can hold safely.
It tells the least number of nails needed to build a frame.
It shows how far to rotate a board round its mid point.
It shows whether the left and right sides of the stool match.
qs.why: Paragraph 4 explains that a step stool's maximum weight is the most load it can hold.

qs.q: What is the main idea of this reading?
choices: Cutting glass is much harder than carving matching frames out of pine wood.
Builders use math and shape words every day to make neat work.
Approximate guesses are always better than exact numbers in a wood shop.
Every piece of wood work must have symmetry and four right corners.
qs.why: The passage shows how builders use perimeter, angles, symmetry, calculation, and limits to make neat work.

clues.text: the full length all the way round the edge
the most load it can hold
the least time it needs to dry
